text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected in us-west-2 streaming tier (svc=inference-stream). SLO breach started at 2026-03-15T14:10:56Z. Metric: p99=3.4s (SLO=1.5s). Cache hitrate for prefix namespace `kv_v3_prefix` dropped to 12% (baseline 78%).

maria: seeing the same in the dashboard. tail stalls ~200ms extra per token, client-side timeouts reported. attaching first logs.

raj: @maria starting live-triage. quick checks: any recent prefix-hash rollouts?

oliver: yes, we deployed prefix-hash v3 to canary->prod at 2026-03-15T13:55Z. rollout completed at 14:02Z. change set: salted hashing + namespace split.

maria: ok likely correlated. low hitrate + new hash => cache misses and heavy backend fanout. impact: increased p99 and streaming stalls. customer CS reports: Acme and Nimbus saw degraded streaming quality and increased 504s.

emily: pinging CS to notify impacted customers and open escalation. template to send: "We're investigating increased latency in US-WEST; mitigation in progress; ETA ~20-30m."

raj: mitigation plan (live):
1) Pause prefix-hash v3 rollout / roll back to v2 mapping (fast).
2) Enable short-term aggressive warmup on hot prefixes (prefetch top keys).
3) Route new streaming requests to fallback model shard (lower perf but stable).
4) Update routes to prefer pod pools with KV-cache warm caches.

maria: I'll take (1) and (3). oliver take (2) and confirm prefetch script. emily handle customer comms. raj coordinate metrics and oncall handoff if needed.

oliver: prefetch script ready in ops/playbooks/prefix_warmup.sh. running now for top-500 prefixes in us-west-2. snippet:```bash
# run from opsctl container
./prefix_warmup.sh --namespace kv_v3_prefix --top 500 --region us-west-2 --concurrency 20
```

oliver: starting now, ETA ~90s to start warming, 5-7m to see hitrate change.

maria: rolling back prefix-hash mapping:```bash
# rollback mapping to v2
redwoodctl routing mappings set --namespace kv_v3_prefix --mapping v2 --confirm
```

maria: issued rollback at 2026-03-15T14:12:40Z. watching cache hitrate and p99.

incident-bot: deployment event: prefix-hash mapping rollback triggered by maria at 2026-03-15T14:12:40Z.

raj: monitoring metrics: pre-rollback p99=3.4s, cache hit=12%. 60s after rollback: cache hit -> 28%, p99 -> 2.1s. still above SLO.

maria: enabling routing fallback for streaming route:```yaml
# minimal
route: streaming-prod
policy: prefer_fallback_shard
max_extra_latency_ms: 200
```

maria: applied at 14:14:02Z.

oliver: prefetch warmed ~80/500 prefixes so far. observed hitrate bump for warmed prefixes to ~70%. running remainder.

raj: metrics update 14:17Z: overall cache hit 42%, p99 1.65s, p95 0.9s. p99 still slightly above SLO but trending down. no new customer 504s in last 4m.

emily: CS message sent to impacted customers (Acme, Nimbus) at 14:18Z. included mitigation steps and ETA.

maria: good. plan next: keep prefetch running for 15m, monitor p99 for stabilization, start a short-lived traffic bake (increase canary weight slowly) if stable.

oliver: note: the root cause appears to be namespace salt change in v3 that redistributed hot keys across buckets; cold caches + downstream fanout created tail stalls. we should add runbook item: require warmup or shadow rehashing when changing salt.

raj: agreed. creating incident ticket in JIRA: INF-2026-298 (latency spike - prefix-hash v3). attaching timeline and metrics.

maria: summary for handoff:
- incident start 14:10:56Z (p99 breach)
- action: rollback mapping (14:12:40Z), prefetch warmup (14:13-ongoing), route fallback (14:14:02Z)
- current state 14:20Z: p99=1.45s (within SLO), cache hit 68% after warmups on hot prefixes, customers notified.

maria: tagging next oncall @raj for continuous monitoring and postmortem ownership. I'll sign off in 15m.

raj: ack. taking over monitoring. will collect logs and confirm reduced error surface. preparing RCA draft: focus on rollout gating, warmup requirement, and telemetry gap on early hitrate drop.

support-bot: Note: customer tickets #C-4421 (Acme) and #C-4478 (Nimbus) updated with status and mitigation notes.

emily: I'll follow-up with customers with a post-incident note once RCA is ready.

maria: thanks all. reactions: :thumbsup: :hourglass_flowing_sand:
